summary: Ciphering Mode Command has Start Ciphering (SC) = 0 - the network explicitly instructed NO ciphering on this channel. This is the A5/0 (null cipher) IMSI-catcher signature: traffic on this dedicated channel is plaintext over the air, and the handset has no way to detect or refuse this network-side choice.
expected: Start Ciphering (SC) = 1 with a non-null Algorithm Identifier (A5/1 or stronger), unless this network deliberately never ciphers by policy (itself worth confirming, not assuming).
spec_citation: 3GPP TS 44.018 clause 3.4.7 and clause 10.5.2.9 (Cipher Mode Setting IE, SC bit); docs/DETECTION-SIGNALS.md signal #11

summary: 1 Identity Request(s) soliciting IMSI observed on the Um interface - the network asked for the permanent identity in the clear, unprotected Layer 3 signalling, the textbook IMSI-catcher technique. Check whether the subscriber already held a valid TMSI at the time (see the paired Location Updating Request/Accept in the same capture) - re-asking a subscriber who already has a valid TMSI is the strongest version of this signature.
expected: Fewer than 1 Identity Request(s) soliciting IMSI per capture window under normal operation.
spec_citation: 3GPP TS 24.008 clause 4.3.3 (Identity Request procedure, sent as plain/unprotected Layer 3 signalling); docs/DETECTION-SIGNALS.md signal #12

summary: IMSI appeared in the clear on the Um interface in 1 frame(s) (1 distinct subscriber(s)). Pre-ciphering GSMTAP capture means this is exactly what a passive Um-interface observer (a real IMSI catcher, or this lab's own legitimate analysis tooling) would also see.
expected: IMSI concealed (TMSI used) except on a legitimate first-ever attach or a genuine Identity Request.
